subsystems.name: Quantum processor
subsystems.role: hosts the encoded gauge fields and matter as quantum states.

subsystems.name: Gauge-field encoding
subsystems.role: maps gauge links and matter onto qubits or qudits while respecting local constraints.

subsystems.name: Time evolution
subsystems.role: drives real-time dynamics of the lattice gauge theory.

subsystems.name: Measurement and readout
subsystems.role: extracts physical observables such as Wilson loops, string tension and particle masses.

subsystems.name: Error mitigation and correction
subsystems.role: reduces the effect of noise on simulation results.

subsystems.name: Classical co-processing and validation
subsystems.role: compares small-system results against exact classical methods.

buildSteps.title: Choose the gauge theory and lattice
buildSteps.detail: Select a model — for example U(1) or SU(2) — and discretise it on a 1D or 2D lattice using a Kogut-Susskind Hamiltonian.

buildSteps.title: Encode degrees of freedom
buildSteps.detail: Map gauge links and matter fields onto qubits or qudits, truncating the infinite-dimensional link Hilbert space and imposing the Gauss law as constraints or penalty terms.

buildSteps.title: Design constraint-preserving circuits or analog Hamiltonian
buildSteps.detail: Build Trotter steps or native interactions that keep the state within the gauge-invariant subspace throughout the evolution.

buildSteps.title: Implement on quantum hardware
buildSteps.detail: Compile the sequence for a trapped-ion, superconducting or neutral-atom platform, calibrating gates and readout for the required fidelity.

buildSteps.title: Validate on small systems classically
buildSteps.detail: Compare results for a few sites in 1D against exact diagonalisation or tensor network calculations to confirm the encoding and evolution are correct.

buildSteps.title: Run real-time dynamics
buildSteps.detail: Prepare an initial state, quench the Hamiltonian and measure observables such as string breaking, hadron masses or thermalisation.

buildSteps.title: Apply error mitigation
buildSteps.detail: Use symmetry verification, zero-noise extrapolation and other techniques to reduce noise and extrapolate to the ideal result.

buildSteps.title: Scale to larger lattices and higher dimensions
buildSteps.detail: Increase qubit count and connectivity to move from 1D chains to 2D grids, and eventually toward 3D.

buildSteps.title: Integrate error correction
buildSteps.detail: Replace physical qubits with fault-tolerant logical qubits to simulate real quantum chromodynamics over long times.

prerequisites.tech: Quantum computing hardware with high-fidelity gates
prerequisites.why: current devices have limited qubit counts, connectivity and coherence times; better fidelity is needed for larger lattices.
gauge fields are infinite-dimensional, so truncation and encoding schemes are an active area of research.
near-term devices require mitigation, while large-scale simulations need fault-tolerant error correction that does not yet exist for this scale.
exact diagonalisation and tensor networks provide benchmarks for small systems and help design the quantum algorithm.

prerequisites.tech: Theory of lattice gauge theories and the sign problem
prerequisites.why: the mathematical framework and the classical sign problem that motivates quantum simulation are well established.

prerequisites.tech: Scalable control and readout for many qubits
prerequisites.why: 2D and 3D lattices demand individual control and readout of hundreds to thousands of qubits with low crosstalk.

pathway.milestone: small-scale simulations of 1D gauge theories on 10–20 qubits across trapped-ion, superconducting and Rydberg platforms
pathway.unlocks: proof-of-principle for real-time dynamics such as string breaking and the Schwinger model.

pathway.milestone: 2D simulations with tens of qubits and improved error mitigation
pathway.unlocks: study of confinement, thermalisation and phase transitions beyond 1D.

pathway.milestone: early fault-tolerant demonstrations for simple gauge models such as U(1) in 2D
pathway.unlocks: longer time dynamics and larger lattices with reliable results.

pathway.milestone: error-corrected quantum simulation of SU(3) quantum chromodynamics in 3+1 dimensions
pathway.unlocks: first-principles calculations of nuclear and particle physics, including neutron-star matter and early-universe conditions.
